# Live demo: an instructor's script {#sec-live-demo}

A step-by-step script for demonstrating this guide live, in about 40 minutes.
It's written to be **foolproof**: everything is rehearsed the day before,
every step has a check ("you should see"), and every step has a plan B, so a slow
network or a typo never stops the class.

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false, "flowchart": {"htmlLabels": false}}}%%
flowchart LR
  subgraph A1["Act 1 · browser · 10 min"]
    P["Paper"] --> G["GEO<br/>GSE52778"] --> RS["SRA Run Selector<br/>metadata + accession list"] --> E["ENA view<br/>same runs"]
  end
  subgraph A2["Act 2 · terminal · 20 min"]
    PF["prefetch"] --> V["vdb-validate"] --> F["fasterq-dump"] --> Z["compress"] --> C["count reads<br/>vs the archive"]
  end
  subgraph A3["Act 3 · scale · 5 min"]
    S["many runs:<br/>submit_each.sh"] --> M["find_missing.sh<br/>→ retry"]
  end
  A1 --> A2 --> A3 --> W(["Wrap-up · 5 min"])
```

## The plan in one table

| Act | Time | What learners see | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Find the data | 10 min | Paper → GEO → SRA Run Selector → ENA, in a browser | airway, [GSE52778](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE52778) |
| 2. Download one run | 20 min | `prefetch` → `vdb-validate` → `fasterq-dump` → compress → check | **SRR390728**: NCBI's own small test run (7.2 M read pairs, 2 × 36 bp) |
| 3. Many runs | 5 min | How to scale up and retry failures | the scripts in `scripts/` |
| Wrap-up | 5 min | Recap map; questions | |

::: {.callout-note}
## Why a different run for Act 2?

An airway run is ~2.9 Gb of sequence: converting it live takes long enough to
lose the room. SRR390728 is the run NCBI uses in its own documentation. It's
small, stable, paired-end RNA-seq, and each step finishes in seconds to a
minute or two. Say so out loud: "the commands are identical for the airway runs;
this one is just smaller."
:::

## What you need

- A laptop or a cluster session with the **SRA Toolkit 3.x**, `pigz` (or `gzip`)
  and `curl`. The easiest: `conda create -n sra -c conda-forge -c bioconda sra-tools pigz`
  ([Setup](setup.qmd)).
- This repository, cloned to your home folder: `git clone https://github.com/jpflores-13/download-public-data.git ~/download-public-data`
- ~5 GB free disk where you'll demo.
- A browser, and a projector-friendly terminal (see below).

## The day before (30–45 min) {#day-before}

Do all of this on **the same computer and account** you'll present from.

1. **Install and activate the tools.**

   ```bash
   conda activate sra          # or: module load <sra module> pigz
   fasterq-dump --version      # 3.x
   ```

2. **Configure the toolkit once**, so `prefetch` saves into the current folder:

   ```bash
   vdb-config --prefetch-to-cwd
   ```

   If a first-run message asks you to run `vdb-config -i`, do it, then *Save*,
   *Exit* (on a cluster: `vdb-config --interactive-mode textual`).

3. **Run the rehearsal**, which is also your **plan B**: it does the whole of
   Act 2 into `~/demo_backup` and prints how long each step took.

   ```bash
   cd ~/download-public-data
   bash demo/make_backup.sh
   ```

   Write the times down. If any step takes more than ~3 minutes on your network,
   plan to switch to the backup for that step during class.

4. **Run the preflight check**:

   ```bash
   bash ~/download-public-data/demo/preflight.sh
   ```

   Every line should say **OK** (a **WARN** about ENA is fine; Act 1 can show
   ENA in the browser). Fix anything marked **FIX** and run it again.

5. **Prepare the browser**: open these tabs, in order, and leave them open:

   1. The paper's data statement (Himes *et al.*, *PLoS One* 2014), or just the
      [GEO page](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE52778)
   2. [SRA Run Selector for GSE52778](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Traces/study/?acc=GSE52778)
   3. [ENA: PRJNA229998](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/browser/view/PRJNA229998)
   4. This guide's [Choose your route](../index.qmd#choose-your-route) map

   Also click **Metadata** and **Accession List** in Run Selector now, and
   move the two files into the backup, in case NCBI's website is slow in class:

   ```bash
   mv ~/Downloads/SraRunTable.csv ~/Downloads/SRR_Acc_List.txt ~/demo_backup/
   ```

   Then **empty your browser's Downloads folder of any other copies**, so the
   live download in class saves under the standard names (not `SRR_Acc_List (1).txt`).

6. **Prepare the terminal** for a projector:
   - Font size 20–24 pt; a light theme often projects better than a dark one.
   - A short prompt, so long paths don't wrap: `export PS1='\$ '` (bash) or
     `PROMPT='%# '` (zsh).
   - Close other terminal tabs; turn off notifications (Do Not Disturb).

7. **Print or open this page** on a second screen or phone, so you can follow
   the script without leaving the terminal.

## 15 minutes before class

```bash
conda activate sra                    # or module load ...
cd ~/                                 # or your cluster scratch folder
rm -rf ~/demo_live && mkdir -p ~/demo_live && cd ~/demo_live
bash ~/download-public-data/demo/preflight.sh
clear
```

All **OK**? You're ready. Keep `~/demo_backup` untouched.

## Act 1: find the data (browser, 10 min) {#act-1}

| # | Do | Say | You should see | If it fails |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.1 | Show the paper's data statement / tab 1 | "Every paper points to an accession. Here it's a GEO series, GSE52778." | GEO page with title, summary, 16 samples | Use a screenshot, or say what it would show |
| 1.2 | On GEO, scroll to **Samples** | "Each GSM is one biological **sample**. GEO holds descriptions and processed files; the raw reads live in SRA." | `GSM1275862 N61311_untreated`, ... | |
| 1.3 | Scroll to the bottom: *Relations → SRA*; then tab 2 (Run Selector) | "Run Selector is the table we actually want: one row per **run**." | Table with `Run`, `LibraryLayout`, `AvgSpotLen`, `Bytes`, `treatment` | Open `~/demo_backup/SraRunTable.csv` in a spreadsheet |
| 1.4 | Point at `Run`, `Experiment`, `BioSample` columns | "Sample → library (SRX) → run (SRR). Runs are what we download." ([Sample, library, run](accessions.qmd#sample-library-run)) | | |
| 1.5 | Point at `LibraryLayout` = PAIRED and `AvgSpotLen` = 126 | "Paired-end, 2 × 63 bp. Spot length counts both reads." | | |
| 1.6 | Click **Metadata** and **Accession List** (Total row) | "Two files to always save: the table, and the list of runs. They land in Downloads; in a moment we'll move them into the dataset folder." | `SraRunTable.csv`, `SRR_Acc_List.txt` in your Downloads | Use the copies in `~/demo_backup/` (step 2.1) |
| 1.7 | Tab 3 (ENA) | "The same runs are mirrored at ENA, which also offers ready-made `.fastq.gz` with checksums." | *Read Files* table with FASTQ links | Skip; mention it |
| 1.8 | Tab 4 (route map) | "Two ways to get the reads: the SRA Toolkit, or ENA. Today: the toolkit." | | |

## Act 2: download one run (terminal, 20 min) {#act-2}

Type every command; don't paste. Typing at the class's pace is the point.
After each command, wait, and read the output aloud.

### 2.1 The dataset folder, and the two files (2 min)

```bash
pwd                                   # ~/demo_live: our dataset folder
mv ~/Downloads/SRR_Acc_List.txt ~/Downloads/SraRunTable.csv .
ls
wc -l SRR_Acc_List.txt                # 16 runs
head -3 SRR_Acc_List.txt
head -2 SraRunTable.csv
```

**Say:** "One folder per dataset. The run list and the metadata live at the top
of it, and every command runs from here. On a cluster, you'd `scp` these two
files up from your laptop instead
([Where to put the two files](finding-data.qmd#where-files-go)).
This folder needs room to spare: conversion needs 10–20 times the download's size."

**Expect:** both files listed; 16 lines in the list, starting `SRR10395...`.
**If `mv` says no such file:** `cp ~/demo_backup/SRR_Acc_List.txt ~/demo_backup/SraRunTable.csv .`

**Say:** "The scripts would read this list to download all 16. To keep the demo
short, we'll download one small test run by hand; the commands are identical."

### 2.2 How big is it? (1 min)

```bash
vdb-dump --info SRR390728 | head -20
```

**Expect:** a block of details including size and spot count.
**If it fails or hangs >30 s:** press `Ctrl-C` and say "the Run Selector's `Bytes`
column tells you the same thing."

### 2.3 Download with prefetch (2–3 min)

```bash
prefetch SRR390728 --max-size u -p
ls -lh SRR390728/
```

**Say:** "`prefetch` downloads NCBI's compressed `.sra` file into a folder named
after the run. `--max-size u` lifts the 20 GB default limit. If the network
drops, run the same command again and it resumes."

**Expect:** progress, then `'SRR390728' was downloaded successfully`; a folder
`SRR390728/` with `SRR390728.sra` (or `.sralite`).

**If it's slow (> your rehearsal time + 1 min) or fails:** `Ctrl-C`, then:

```bash
cp -r ~/demo_backup/sra/SRR390728 .
```

"This is exactly why we rehearse with a backup. And it's what happens in real
life: downloads fail, you retry."

### 2.4 Check it (1 min)

```bash
vdb-validate SRR390728
```

**Expect:** several `... is consistent` / `ok` lines, no `error`.
**Say:** "A cheap check before an expensive conversion."

### 2.5 Convert to FASTQ (2–3 min)

```bash
mkdir -p tmp fastq
fasterq-dump SRR390728 --threads 4 --temp tmp --outdir fastq --progress
ls -lh fastq/
```

**Say while it runs:** "`fasterq-dump` reads the `.sra` and writes FASTQ. It
splits pairs into `_1` and `_2`: that's `--split-3`, the default. Any reads
without a mate would go to a third file; this run has none."

**Expect:** `fastq/SRR390728_1.fastq` and `fastq/SRR390728_2.fastq`, roughly 1 GB each.

**If it fails with a disk message:** `df -h .`, then use the backup:
`cp ~/demo_backup/fastq/SRR390728_* fastq/` and skip 2.6.

### 2.6 Compress (1–2 min)

```bash
pigz -p 4 fastq/*.fastq        # or: gzip fastq/*.fastq
ls -lh fastq/
```

**Say:** "`fasterq-dump` doesn't compress. Compare the sizes before and after:
FASTQ shrinks several-fold."

### 2.7 Look inside (2 min)

```bash
zcat fastq/SRR390728_1.fastq.gz | head -8      # macOS: gzip -dc fastq/SRR390728_1.fastq.gz | head -8
```

**Say:** walk through the four lines of one read: name (`@SRR390728.1 ...`),
bases, `+`, qualities. "The original instrument names are replaced by
`run.spot`. Read length 36."

### 2.8 Is it all there? (2 min)

```bash
for f in fastq/*.fastq.gz; do echo "$f $(( $(gzip -dc $f | wc -l) / 4 ))"; done
```

**Expect:** both files **7178576** reads.
**Say:** "Same number in `_1` and `_2`, and it matches the archive's spot
count (7,178,576 on Run Selector or ENA). That's the check that matters most."

### 2.9 The ENA shortcut (2 min)

```bash
curl -s https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR390/SRR390728/SRR390728_1.fastq.gz | gzip -dc | head -8
```

**Say:** "ENA serves the same reads as `.fastq.gz` directly. Here I'm only
streaming the first two reads; `scripts/ena_download.sh` downloads whole runs and
checks their MD5s. No toolkit, no conversion."

**If it hangs > 20 s:** `Ctrl-C`; "ENA is busy; this is why we have two routes."

### 2.10 Tidy up (1 min)

```bash
rm -rf SRR390728 tmp
ls
```

**Say:** "Once the FASTQ is checked, the `.sra` and the temporary files can go."

## Act 3: many runs (terminal, 5 min) {#act-3}

Don't run downloads here: show the scripts and the retry idea.

```bash
cd ~/download-public-data
less scripts/submit_each.sh        # q to quit
```

**Say:** "For 50 runs we loop the same steps: one cluster job per run (or an
array job, or a simple loop on a laptop)." Show the [Downloading many runs](at-scale.qmd)
route map.

Then show the retry loop on something real:

```bash
cd ~/demo_live
printf "SRR390728\nSRR1039508\n" > demo_list.txt
bash ~/download-public-data/scripts/find_missing.sh demo_list.txt fastq > failed.txt
cat failed.txt
```

**Expect:** `SRR1039508: no FASTQ` on screen, and `failed.txt` containing `SRR1039508`.
**Say:** "Downloads fail now and then. We don't search logs: we check which outputs
are missing, resubmit just those, and repeat until the list is empty."

## Wrap-up (5 min) {#wrap-up}

Show the [Choose your route](../index.qmd#choose-your-route) map once more and recap:

1. **Find**: paper → GEO → Run Selector: save the metadata table and the run list **at the top of the dataset folder**.
2. **Download**: `prefetch` → `vdb-validate` → `fasterq-dump` → compress (or ENA).
3. **Check**: read counts match the archive; `_1` = `_2`.
4. **Organise**: merge runs of the same library; name files by sample; keep the metadata.

Point learners to the [Worked example](worked-example.qmd) to do the full
airway download themselves, and the [Cheat sheet](cheatsheet.qmd).

## Plan B, all in one place {#plan-b}

| Problem | Do this | Say |
|---|---|---|
| NCBI website slow (Act 1) | Open `~/demo_backup/SraRunTable.csv` | "Same table I saved yesterday" |
| `prefetch` slow / fails | `Ctrl-C`; `cp -r ~/demo_backup/sra/SRR390728 .` | "Downloads fail: retry, or here's one I made earlier" |
| `fasterq-dump` slow / disk full | `Ctrl-C`; `cp ~/demo_backup/fastq/SRR390728_* fastq/` | "Conversion needs lots of temp space" |
| `command not found` | `conda activate sra` (or `module load ...`) | "Every new terminal needs the environment" |
| No internet at all | Run Act 2 from the backup: `cd ~/demo_backup` and show each step's output with `ls -lh`, `zcat ... \| head`, the read-count loop | "Here's what each step produced" |
| You mistype | Up-arrow, fix, Enter | (Learners like seeing this; it's normal) |

## After class

```bash
rm -rf ~/demo_live          # keep ~/demo_backup for next time
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## For learners following along

Learners can type along on their own machine if they have the toolkit
([Setup](setup.qmd)). SRR390728 needs ~3 GB free while converting. If a learner's
download is slow, have them use the ENA streaming command (2.9) to see real
reads while they wait.
:::
